claim: A 3 m rake with a full heap of about 231 kg needs about 2.75 kN to drag (0.9 kN per metre)
law: Coulomb sliding of the heap (friction 0.70, tan of the 35 degree repose angle) plus an assumed 300 N/m to loosen the harvest layer and skid friction 0.30; granular drag in front of a blade (soil-tool mechanics)
check: heap 1589 N + layer 900 N + skids 259 N = 2748 N; the layer term is an estimate, not a measurement (SDG-CAL-001 [A7] rests on the assumed 300 N/m; measured on the partner's bed (SDG-DEC-001, to confirm 7))

claim: At the design drag of S1, two people at 89 N each on 330 mm cranks wind the rake
law: Torque balance through a 6 to 1 spur stage, 94 % gear and bearing efficiency, rope on its third layer; if the drag is 1.5 times the estimate the pull rises 1.42 times and the skids are raised or the rake shortened (SDG-CAL-001 [A10])

claim: Two people at 120 N give at least 3 kN of rope pull, even on a full drum
law: Torque balance as S2 on the fourth layer (largest radius)

claim: The anchored capstan does not tip, even at twice the rated pull
law: Moments about the front tips of the runners: rope at 677 mm against weight, chain tension and chain line, both chains taut (rated pull 1.56); a slack chain is a hazard controlled by the turnbuckles and the set-up check (SDG-RSK-001 F11)

claim: The crank shaft survives a season of rotating bending at the rated pull
law: Goodman, fully reversed bending from the tooth force and steady torque at the 25 mm step (notch factor 1.6), C45+QT (UTS 650 MPa), surface and size factors, endurance halved for bare steel in salt air (corrosion fatigue, estimate)

claim: The gear and ratchet keys carry the drum torque at 6 kN with a margin of 2
law: Key bearing stress 2 T / (d (h/2) L), 12 x 8 keys on the 40 mm shaft: gear hub 44 mm (C45+QT, 430 MPa), ratchet with its welded hub 64 mm (C45+N, 305 MPa)

claim: The induction-hardened pinion teeth resist pitting at the rated pull
law: Hertz contact sigma_H = Z_E Z_H sqrt(K_A F_t (u + 1) / (b d u)), K_A 1.25 for hand cranking; allowable about 1,000 MPa for induction-hardened C45 teeth (estimate)

claim: The rake does not pitch onto its blade edge under the full heap
law: Moments about the skid tips: the pull at the bridle height (70 mm) against the heap at a third of the blade height, the layer at the edge and skid friction at the floor; restoring moment of the rake's weight about the skid tips

claim: With two 24 kg ballast bags the blade stays down until about 3.5 m from the bund toe
law: Vertical equilibrium of the rake under the rising rope: lift-off when T sin(theta) exceeds the rake's weight

claim: The skids press on the pan floor less than a worker standing on it does
law: Contact pressure = weight / skid area; the pull's pitching moment is small with the bridles at the skid foot (S29), so the pressure stays near the static value; a 70 kg person on two feet (about 0.025 m2 each) presses 13.7 kPa

claim: The 40 mm drum shaft keeps a margin of 2 at twice the rated pull (6 kN)
law: Bending (rope load and the gear's reaction, both planes) plus torsion, von Mises; C45+QT yield 430 MPa, 16 to 40 mm (EN 10083-2)

claim: The crank shaft at the bearing next to the overhung pinion keeps a margin of 2 at twice the rated pull (6 kN)
law: Bending from the full tooth force plus torsion, von Mises, 30 mm; C45+QT yield 430 MPa

claim: The module 4 pinion teeth keeps a margin of 2 at twice the rated pull (6 kN)
law: Lewis bending, form factor 0.277 for 14 teeth; C45+N yield 305 MPa above 16 mm

claim: The pawl boss welded to the cheek keeps a margin of 2 at twice the rated pull (6 kN)
law: Cantilever bending of the 40 mm boss; S275 yield 275 MPa (EN 10025-2)

claim: The 3 m FRP rake beam keeps a margin of 2 at twice the rated pull (6 kN)
law: Simply supported beam under the heap and layer load; pultruded FRP flexural strength 200 MPa (lower bound)

claim: The drum barrel is not crushed by three layers of rope wound on at 6 kN, with a margin of 2
law: Hoop stress of a ring under rope pressure, sigma = k T / (t s); 168.3 x 6.3 YSt 310 tube, yield 310 MPa (IS 4923); the multi-layer factor k = 1.8 for three loaded layers is taken from wire-rope practice and is not sourced for polyester (independent review); the margin of 2 holds for k up to 1.95; flange thrust not yet checked
check: 143 MPa against 155 MPa at k = 1.8 (margin 2.17); the 4.5 mm pipe it replaces failed at about 200 MPa (sourced layer factor and a CalRig proof load with three layers wound on (TRL 4); SDG-DEC-001 D18)

claim: A hand force of 150 N or less on the band brake holds the rated pull, with the lining wet
law: Band brake (capstan) equation T1/T2 = exp(mu theta), mu 0.20 for a woven lining wet with brine (0.30 dry), 247 degrees of wrap, differential lever 600 mm with a 50 mm inner arm

claim: The more loaded anchor chain keeps a margin of 2 on its working load limit at 6 kN
law: Chain tension from the 23 degree chain line with 70 % of the pull on one chain (unequal tension, independent review); 10 mm grade 30 chain working load limit 11.8 kN (2,650 lb, catalogue class, to confirm on purchase)

claim: Each 150 mm helical anchor holds at least 1.5 times its share of the rated pull in the ground behind the bund
law: Deep helix bearing Q = 9 s_u A in firm clay, s_u 50 kPa assumed; the rod is screwed in at 45 degrees and the chain arrives at 23 degrees, so the load is 22 degrees off the anchor's axis; at a helix depth of about 0.6 m the bearing factor may be below 9, and saline silty soil can be softer
check: 7.95 kN estimated against a proof pull of 3.42 kN (1.5 times a 70 % share); 1.74 times the 6 kN chain force at a 70 % share; soil unknown (SDG-CAL-001 [C10]; site pull test before first use (SDG-DEC-001, to confirm 6))

claim: The rope's minimum breaking strength after splices is at least 5 times the rated pull
law: Working-load factor of 5 to 12 for fibre rope in general use (rope makers' practice); 12 mm polyester double braid 27 kN class, splices 85 %
check: 7.65 MBS / rated pull >= 5 MBS / rated pull

claim: The rope lasts a season over the 100 mm roller and the 168 mm drum and dragging on the bed
law: Rope makers give a minimum sheave-to-rope diameter ratio of about 8 for polyester double braid (to confirm on the chosen rope's datasheet); a bend at D/d 8.3 costs about 15 % of strength (the working-load factor falls from 7.7 to about 6.5, still over 5); salt crystals abrade the rope where it lies on the bed on the light return
check: roller 8.3, drum 14.0 against about 8; abrasion life unknown (rope datasheet on purchase (SDG-DEC-001, to confirm 10); daily inspection (SDG-RSK-001 F1))

claim: Every bolted joint can be assembled: washers and nuts clear their neighbours, holes keep at least 1.2 diameters of edge
law: Edge distance e >= 1.2 d0 (EN 1993-1-8 practice); interference check of every part at detail level D3 (.kit/cad_check.py)
check: cross-tube bolts at 36 mm on 100 x 80 plates (14 mm edge, 1.27 d0), guard spacer holes 73 mm from the cheek edge, axle split pins outside the plates, gear and ratchet hubs clear of the bearings, guard and crank; cad/fidelity.json: no interference

claim: At the design drag, each of two crankers works within a sustained rate, even at the end of a pass
law: Rope power over efficiency, shared by two, with the rope on its third layer at 23 turns a minute (mean over a pass 64 W; pull duty about 45 %); sustained hand-cranking by an average adult about 75 W (.kit/stem_check.py limit)

claim: Winding at about 70 W is safe in the harvest heat with work planned for the cooler hours
law: Arm cranking is about 15 % efficient, so 64 to 71 W of external work is a metabolic rate of about 450 to 500 W, high work; ISO 7243 sets a reference WBGT of about 26 C for acclimatised workers at high work (to confirm against the 2017 edition); afternoon WBGT in the Little Rann in March and April is likely to exceed it, so 6 working hours a day (S24) may be optimistic
check: safe in the early morning and evening only; a work and rest schedule is needed (work hours, shade and water agreed with the partner (PRB co-design checklist; RSK H6))

claim: Hot-dip galvanised steel on the dry ground lasts more than one season in salt-laden air with a daily rinse
law: Zinc corrosion rate about 4.2 to 8.4 um a year in a very high (C5) atmosphere and up to about 25 um a year in an extreme (CX) one (ISO 9223); minimum mean hot-dip coating 85 um on steel over 6 mm and 55 um on 1.5 to 3 mm (ISO 1461); cut edges and drilled holes are galvanised after fabrication
check: at 25 um a year (brine-wetted, CX): 3.4 years on the 6 mm plate, 2.2 years on the 3 mm runners and tubes; more than one season

claim: 316 stainless fittings on the rake survive a season wetted by near-saturated brine
law: Type 316 suffers pitting and crevice corrosion in warm chloride brines, worst in crevices under bolt heads and washers (Nickel Institute guidance on stainless steel in seawater); daily freshwater rinse lowers the risk
check: no calculation possible; crevice corrosion of the blade and hanger bolts is the likely failure (season trial with inspection (PR-007, TRL 5); duplex 2205 bolts as the fallback (RSK F9))

claim: UHMW-PE, pultruded FRP and polyester rope keep their strength in brine and sun for a season
law: Polyolefins and glass-polyester or vinylester composites are inert to sodium chloride; UV degrades unstabilised UHMW-PE and bare FRP surfaces, so the BOM asks for UV-stabilised UHMW-PE and a surfacing veil on the FRP
check: chemically inert; UV handled by grade choice

claim: No metal coating, paint, grease or FRP touches the salt
law: The salt touches only the UHMW-PE blade and skids (food-contact grades exist), 316 stainless and the polyester rope; no zinc, paint, grease or FRP is in the pan below the blade top; the rope may shed fibres where it drags on the bed (to watch in trials)
check: material list by inspection of the model

claim: At the design drag, one set gathers about 532 kg of salt an hour with a crew of four
law: One full heap per strip over pull, return and move times

claim: One set gathers about 195 t in a 61-day harvest, about a third of one family pan's yearly output (6 cooler hours a day; about 130 t at 4 h)
law: Rate x 61 days x 6 cooler hours; a family pan yields 500 to 600 t a year (Business Standard, 2009)

claim: Each drum stores the 45 m of rope a 30 m pan needs
law: Turns per layer x layer circumference, four layers of 12 mm rope on a 168.3 mm barrel

claim: A team of 14 walking haulers draws a 1.5 m rake at 1.73 kN (option B)
law: Sustained walking pull of about 130 N per person, the order of the maximum acceptable sustained pull forces for most adult women (Snook and Ciriello, 1991); rope pull from the drag model of S1 at half width
check: 14 x 130 N >= 1729 N; possible, but the crew is large

claim: A post on four 25 mm stakes holds the 90 degree rope turn (option B)
law: Resultant of the turned rope, 1.41 times the pull, at 0.76 m height; lateral capacity of short stakes in clay
check: 2.44 kN at 0.76 m; stake capacity depends on the soil

claim: Two people at about 140 N on a 10 to 1 hand lever pull the 3 m rake (option C)
law: Lever ratio 1052 / 81 mm, 85 % efficiency at pins and jaws, the rope pull of SDG-CAL-001 [A8]
check: 136 N per person <= 150 N per person

claim: Cam jaws grip polyester rope without wearing it out within a season (option C)
law: Toothed cam grips cut and glaze fibre rope under repeated slip; commercial fibre-rope pullers use smooth or grooved jaws and limit the load
check: rope wear under 600 strokes a pass is unknown
